o1.biggest_strength: Leads with the $82,000 salary exactly as the brand demands and ties every element (overnight shift, weekend rotation, written-reply application) back to the data with clean, traceable reviewer-hour math.
o1.biggest_mistake: Its exercises test writing well but don't specifically probe how a candidate handles the 00:00-08:00 UTC queue or a system-wide outage, so the 'overnight gap' signal is asserted in the post more than tested in the funnel.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add one shortlist exercise set in the quiet overnight hours (a multi-customer outage at 03:00 UTC) so the scorecard actually measures the gap the hire is meant to close.

o2.biggest_mistake: Buries the $82,000 salary in a 'Pay and terms' paragraph rather than the first screen, which misses a stated brand principle and the owner's explicit 'salary in the first screen' delight.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the $82,000 to the very first line of the post and trim the post slightly so the great exercises and hours table carry more of the weight.

reason: Both are strong and built on the data, but Output 1 leads with the salary as we insist on and shows cleaner, traceable reviewer-hour math, while Output 2's smarter exercises are offset by burying the number and running denser.
